name: OWASP Non-Human Identities Top 10
source_notes: Verified against the OWASP NHI Top 10 project page and its 2025 index (definitions quoted there); repo front-matter shows level 2, type documentation.
caveats: Per-item 2025 detail pages were not read, so official prevention bullets are missing; prevention entries here are reinhardt inferences, partly from the OWASP Secrets Management Cheat Sheet.
The official index "Read More" link for NHI3 points to the NHI2 page; the correct slug is /2025/3-vulnerable-third-party-nhi/.
Only the year 2025 is verified; no exact release date.
The notes attribute no CWEs to NHI items.
Provider key prefixes in detection signals come from vendor docs and gitleaks rules, not OWASP; OpenAI/Anthropic/github_pat_ formats were not confirmed on vendor docs.

items.name: Improper Offboarding
items.summary: Service accounts, access keys and other non-human identities are not deactivated or removed when no longer needed.
prevention: (inferred) Keep an inventory of NHIs with owners.
(inferred) Revoke and delete credentials when a service or integration is retired.
(inferred) Periodically review for unused identities.

static: (inferred) Credentials in config for services no longer referenced in code (weak signal)

items.name: Secret Leakage
items.summary: API keys, tokens, encryption keys and certificates leak to unsanctioned stores across the SDLC, e.g. hard-coded in source, in plaintext config or shared in chat.
prevention: (inferred) Keep secrets in a secrets manager, never in code, images or build-time env.
(inferred) Run secret detection in the IDE, pre-commit and CI.
(inferred) On leak: revoke, then rotate, then delete, then log.
(inferred) Prefer dynamic or short-lived secrets.

static: Known-prefix secrets in source (sk_live_, rk_live_, AKIA, ghp_/github_pat_, xoxb-/xoxp-, sk-ant-, OpenAI sk-, sb_secret_, PEM private keys)
Supabase JWT with "role":"service_role" in client code or NEXT_PUBLIC_/VITE_/EXPO_PUBLIC_ env
Secrets in Dockerfile ENV/ARG, workflow env, Info.plist/.xcconfig/Swift literals
review: Secrets in chat tools, tickets and git history beyond the scanned tree

items.name: Vulnerable Third-Party NHI
items.summary: Third-party integrations such as IDE extensions and SaaS apps hold NHIs; a compromised or malicious update can steal credentials or misuse their permissions.
prevention: (inferred) Vet and govern third-party integrations and extensions.
(inferred) Grant third parties least privilege and review granted permissions.
(inferred) Rotate credentials exposed to a compromised integration.

review: Installed IDE extensions and SaaS OAuth grants

items.name: Insecure Authentication
items.summary: NHIs authenticate with methods that are deprecated, vulnerable to known attacks or otherwise weak.
prevention: (inferred) Prefer modern, short-lived token-based authentication such as OIDC federation.
(inferred) Retire deprecated auth methods and long-lived static keys.

static: (inferred) Static API keys used where OIDC/workload identity is available

items.name: Overprivileged NHI
items.summary: NHIs are granted significantly more privileges than their function requires.
prevention: (inferred) Scope each NHI to the minimum permissions needed.
(inferred) Use publishable/anon keys where a secret key is not required.
(inferred) Review and trim granted permissions regularly.

static: Supabase service_role used where anon/publishable key suffices

items.name: Insecure Cloud Deployment Configurations
items.summary: CI/CD authenticates to cloud providers with static credentials that can leak, or with OIDC whose identity tokens or claim conditions are not validated strictly.
prevention: (inferred) Use OIDC federation instead of static cloud keys in CI.
(inferred) Constrain OIDC trust policies with strict sub and audience conditions.

static: Static AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID in CI instead of aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials role-to-assume
OIDC trust policies with wildcard sub (e.g. repo:*)

items.name: Long-Lived Secrets
items.summary: Secrets have expiration dates far in the future or never expire.
prevention: (inferred) Set short expirations and automate rotation.
(inferred) Prefer temporary credentials (e.g. STS ASIA keys, fine-grained or expiring tokens).

static: Classic ghp_ PATs and AKIA long-lived keys
JWTs with no or far-future exp

items.name: Environment Isolation
items.summary: The same NHIs are reused across development, test, staging and production, especially between testing and production.
prevention: (inferred) Issue separate credentials per environment.
(inferred) Do not use production credentials or data in non-production.

items.name: NHI Reuse
items.summary: A single NHI is shared across different applications, services or components.
prevention: (inferred) Issue a distinct identity per application or service.
(inferred) Scope each identity to its own component.

static: One key value reused across multiple services or config files

items.name: Human Use of NHI
items.summary: People use NHIs for manual tasks, gaining elevated privileges and losing auditability.
prevention: (inferred) Give humans their own identities and audited access.
(inferred) Restrict NHI credentials to automated workloads.

review: Audit logs showing interactive use of service credentials
